nba_directive.reason_text: This client is already engaged and moving toward a purchase — the play calls for speed and a frictionless path to application, not re-selling or discovery. The FHA-with-PMI detail is a useful hook but should not derail the momentum into a full consultation.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Reply immediately and directly to whatever they asked — do not open with a rate pitch or a list of questions
  - Match their energy: they are ready, so your tone should be 'let's get this done' not 'tell me more about your situation'
  - One sentence max of context-setting before moving to the next step

- Surface the FHA/PMI fact as a brief, relevant aside — not a detour
  - They are currently on an FHA loan paying $158/mo in mortgage insurance
  - On the new purchase, note that conventional financing may eliminate PMI depending on down payment — flag it as something to optimize in the application, not a reason to pause and re-evaluate

- Drive straight to the soft credit pull or e-sign application
  - 'I can get you a full picture with no impact to your credit — here's the link: [insert application link]'
  - If they prefer a call, offer one specific short window: 'I have 10 minutes at [time] — does that work?'
  - Do not ask more than one clarifying question before sending the link

- Keep the reply short — three sentences or fewer if possible
  - Over-engaging a hot lead kills conversion; let the application do the work
  - Your job here is to remove friction, not demonstrate expertise
